about: Orders a ruler gives in war and occupation (the user's own lines from September 27 first), with the engine action each must produce on the offline regex path and on the stubbed order-reader path, and the effect in plain words. Rows run in order on one world: Tsaren (300 people, resistance 0.6) held by a garrison of about 39 so that every measure has hands to carry it out (the user's own 16 cannot do all of them at once: guards tied to the bound men and hostages leave no one to watch conscripts, and the war leader says so); the Esurai at war with us. 'retake' re-establishes the garrison after a row that gives the town up. In the reader stubs, ref 'tsaren' becomes town:<id>, 'esurai' people:<id>.

rows.order: Round up all the men of Tsaren and tie them up. If any resist or attempt to flee, threaten their wives and children.
rows.effect: The men of Tsaren are rounded up house to house and bound under guard (bounded by 8 bound men per free guard); a harsh stance: fewer slip away (the rest are recorded as fled for a chase), more dread and grievance, a small chance of a later incident; resistance held under 0.35 while bound; card note 'Men bound and under guard · N'; one Chronicle entry.
A detachment of the free fighters (guards on the bound men stay) goes after the men who slipped away, a day or two out.
The detachment turns back to Tsaren; the garrison stays.
Already bound: the binding runs another month (no second round-up, no stacked effects).
Houses searched for spears, bows and axes; up to 40 kept for our levy (improvised weapons); resistance x0.8 and capped at 0.6 for 90 days; small grievance.
Disarming already in force: the order is renewed, not repeated.

rows.order: Take hostages from their leading families
rows.effect: 2-12 hostages (elders and leading families) held in the garrison house, fed from our stores, 1 guard per 4; resistance x0.75, capped at 0.5 for 90 days; later round-ups lose fewer men.

rows.order: Keep them in their houses after dark
rows.effect: Curfew for 20 days, two of ours walking the lanes; flight halved; welfare and trust dip.
One sweep: hidden weapons, hidden food (to our stores unless lenient), men hiding bound with the rest; resistance -0.05; grievance up.
The men work in gangs on a stake wall and ditch for a month (the bound men if bound); the town's fortification rises a little each day, bounded at +0.15; welfare down, grievance up.
About a third of their stores (bounded by 50 per fighter) comes to our stores and the garrison; the garrison stays; welfare down, grievance up, resistance +0.03.

rows.order: Take their young men into our bands
rows.effect: Up to 30 percent of the men (3 per free guard, at most 40) serve beside the garrison as carriers and watchmen, taken from the bound first, then the work gangs, then the free; some desert each day (fewer under a harsh hand) and reach their people.
The named person (else the garrison's commander) sits over Tsaren as headman in our name; their elders lose their say; resistance -0.04, local institutions -0.1.
5-40 of our families take up the empty houses under the garrison's protection (still counted as our people); integration +0.05, grievance up.
A week of half rations from our stores (bounded at 400) and our men's hands kept off them: welfare and trust up, grievance and resistance down, opinion and mercy up, the court's love a little up.
Relief already in force: renewed, not repeated.

The few who led the fighting (1-6, about 5 percent of the men) are put to death before the town; resistance -0.15 now and capped at 0.45 for 30 days; grievance +0.18, dread and grudges; never every man.

rows.order: Threaten their families if they run
rows.effect: A standing harsh word to the garrison: any man who runs, his family answers for it; resistance -0.05, grievance and dread up, an incident chance.

rows.order: If any of the men resist, kill them
rows.effect: A standing brutal word: any man who fights or runs is killed; nobody is killed now; dread up, a higher incident chance.

rows.order: Make them understand who rules now
rows.effect: A harder hand: spears in the lanes, beatings for talking back; resistance down a little, grievance up.
Grave and unclear: ONE question with concrete choices (put to death only the few who led them, bind the men, take their food); nothing is done yet.
Said again without an answer: the war leader's nearest reading is carried out, never the same question again.
The hostages go home; grievance -0.04, trust +0.05, mercy.
The bound men are untied and sent home; the resistance cap lifts and resistance rebounds +0.08; the card note goes back.
They may go out after dark again.
Words that name no measure and no tone: the garrison's plain standing word (keep order, harm nobody who does not raise a hand), a tiny bounded effect; never 'it is already ours'.

rows.order: Put the men to work in the fields
rows.effect: Labour already running: renewed and turned to the fields; their harvest feeds the garrison and our stores, bounded at 300.
Everything: up to 60 percent of what is left; they go hungry (welfare -0.15), grievance +0.12.
An attack on a town we hold: the war leader says it is already ours and who holds it; no march.

rows.order: Send our full forces against Tsaren
rows.effect: Said again: the same truth in different words, and no question he already asked.
Military government through the occupation policy, or the plain reason the garrison is too few to hold 300 down.
Spared and held: grievance -0.1, trust +0.1, mercy.
A band standing at the town joins the garrison, or the plain reason none can.

rows.order: Kill all the males and take the women and girls to Seanstone
rows.effect: Every bound man is put to death (none can run; the garrison's hands set only how long it takes) and any free men are each caught on the stated odds, the rest running; the women and girls are each rounded up on the stated odds and walked home as captives (4 per fighter); every count lands in the town's ledger; dread, grudges, cohesion and legitimacy costs.

rows.order: I want you to kill all the males of Tsaren immediately
rows.effect: The men who remain are put to death; with none left (the row above killed them all), an honest refusal that says who is still in the town. Never anyone in the hall.
Bands in the field turn home; the war leader asks once whether to leave Tsaren unguarded.
The garrison stays.

rows.order: Burn what remains of Tsaren to the ground
rows.effect: Tsaren burned, its people scattered, the garrison comes home; measures end with it.
Self-rule restored; the garrison marches home.

rows.order: Take tribute from Tsaren and leave
rows.effect: What the band can carry of their stores, then home; not a requisition (the town is left).
